The program

Platform / SINCHDrone

Vertical flight.
A broader mission.

SINCH brings a fixed-wing airframe and vertical propulsion into a shared development platform for flight control, autonomy, and endurance research.

Platform brief

Configuration
VTOL fixed-wing aircraft
Near-term focus
Hover stability and control
Integration work
Ground systems and energy

Control before transition.

Reliable hover is a necessary foundation for the wider aircraft program. The next design decisions depend on understanding how the wing, propulsion system, mass distribution, and flight controller interact.

Configuration measurements and flight-test evidence can distinguish aerodynamic loading from control, structural, or propulsion effects. That work informs the route toward transition and forward-flight evaluation.

Current development objective: establish repeatable, controlled hover before progressing to transition testing.

Integrated by design

The aircraft also provides a context for investigating autonomous landing, battery interfaces, and solar assistance. These are connected development objectives rather than independent demonstrations.

Ground systems

The mission continues
after landing.

Robotic ground support explores how an aircraft can align, exchange energy, and prepare for another flight.

Robotic Ground Station

The aircraft–ground interface.

Landing alignment, battery handling, and electrical connections must function as a coordinated system. The program develops these interfaces through mechanical design, sensing, and subsystem testing.

The long-term objective is autonomous battery exchange. Repeatable individual operations are the foundation for an integrated demonstration.

01 / Alignment

Position the aircraft.

Develop the landing and mechanical interfaces that bring the aircraft into a repeatable position.

02 / Handling

Move the battery.

Evaluate transfer mechanisms, retention, and the fit between battery hardware and airframe.

03 / Integration

Verify the sequence.

Bring motion, sensing, and power connections together through staged testing.

Aerodynamics & experimentation

Understand the flow.
Inform the design.

Aircraft analysis and wind-tunnel work investigate the aerodynamic interactions that affect performance and control.

Aerodynamic visualization / 2026 showcase archive

Analysis connected
to hardware.

Wing geometry, propulsion placement, and airframe additions all influence the aircraft. The program uses aerodynamic studies to frame design questions and interpret experimental observations.

A SINCH-representative wind-tunnel model supports propulsion-interaction research, including particle image velocimetry (PIV), a method for measuring flow using illuminated particles.

Research focus

Evidence at the right scale.

Model geometry, test conditions, and measurement limits determine how results apply to the aircraft. The aim is to connect observed flow behavior with useful configuration decisions.

← Back to research

Energy & endurance

More useful energy.
Less integration penalty.

Solar assistance is an aircraft-level trade: useful electrical power must be weighed against added mass, packaging, and aerodynamic effects.

Development questions

Electrical
Usable power and regulation
Mechanical
Attachment and wing integration
Aircraft
Mass and endurance effects

The installation matters.

The earlier solar concept used 16 cells or panels with a combined peak rating of 57.6 W. Those design estimates provide a starting point for evaluating the installation, not a claim of demonstrated onboard performance.

Current planning needs to connect the electrical architecture with wing geometry and aircraft control. Any change to panel count or placement must also account for wiring, voltage compatibility, and the effect on mass distribution.

Development objective: verify useful solar output and its net effect on aircraft operation.

Autonomy platform / Storm IV

A testbed for
autonomous landing.

Storm IV supports the development of sensing, control interfaces, and precision-landing behavior before broader aircraft integration.

Develop the behavior.
Evaluate the response.

The quadcopter platform gives the team a setting to develop and test autonomy functions. Landing-target detection and flight-controller integration are part of the wider program’s work.

Repeatability, sensing, and alignment remain important considerations when adapting landing behavior to other aircraft and ground hardware.

The program

Student engineering.
System-level thinking.

BANSHEE UAV is a student aerospace project at California State Polytechnic University, Pomona. Our work connects research with the practical demands of integrated hardware.

How the work comes together

Across disciplines.
Around a shared aircraft.

The program brings aerodynamic analysis, structures, fabrication, electronics, and flight testing into the same design process. Systems engineering connects the requirements and interfaces between them.

Students work through the decisions that make a concept testable: what to measure, how to build it, and what evidence is needed before the next step.

Organization

The subteams.

Specialist work, coordinated through shared interfaces.

01

Aerodynamics

Aircraft performance, stability analysis, and experimental flow research.

02

Design & Structures

Load paths, airframe geometry, structural analysis, and mechanical interfaces.

03

Manufacturing

Composite fabrication, tooling, printed components, and aircraft assembly.

04

Flight Testing & DAQ

Test planning, flight operations, and data acquisition.

05

Avionics / Robotics

Flight electronics, sensing, autonomy, and ground-system development.

06

Systems Engineering

Requirements, schedules, interfaces, risks, and verification planning.

Development / 2026–2027

Progress built
on evidence.

The proposed development sequence prioritizes a serviceable baseline, controlled testing, and verified interfaces. These are planning priorities, not completed milestones.

01PLANNED

Establish the configuration

Record aircraft geometry, mass properties, propulsion hardware, and control settings.

Intended outcome

A consistent baseline for comparison.

02PLANNED

Resolve hover control

Use measured response and controlled tests to investigate instability and evaluate corrections.

Intended outcome

Repeatable, controlled hover.

03PLANNED

Validate subsystem interfaces

Evaluate landing behavior, ground mechanisms, flow research, and the solar architecture.

Intended outcome

Evidence that interfaces work as intended.

04PLANNED

Progress toward integration

Bring the aircraft and supporting systems together through reviewed test stages.

Intended outcome

An integrated demonstration supported by test evidence.

The next step depends
on what the test shows.
